edges.effect_quant: The strongest quantitative studies point in a protective direction, but the pooled magnitude varies across populations and methods.
edges.population: asymptomatic adults undergoing prevention risk stratification
edges.mechanism: Coronary artery calcium scoring plausibly improves cardiovascular risk reclassification through a factor-specific pathway documented in the literature, even if the exact size of benefit varies by population and dose.
edges.summary: The anchor for this edge is the 2021 Matos cohort in Rev Port Cardiol (Engl Ed), which suggests that coronary artery calcium scoring tracks with lower risk or better outcomes for cardiovascular risk reclassification. Later papers point in much the same direction, so the live uncertainty is usually about effect size or which subgroups carry the signal most strongly.
edges.caveats: Healthier-user bias, screening intensity, and baseline risk can all inflate apparent benefit in observational work, so the magnitude should be read conservatively.
